source_text: Imponet manum suam super caput hostiae, et acceptabilis erit. Manus imposita communionem significat: quae offeruntur, nostra fiunt. Christus caput; nos membra. Imponere manum — consentire et confiteri peccata quae in hostiam transeunt. Sanguis adspersus ad altare: sine sanguinis effusione non fit remissio. Pontifex noster Christus semel obtulit seipsum.
thought_title: Laying on of hands and the blood of Christ
orientation: Origen is explaining the ritual of the burnt offering from Leviticus, interpreting each action as a figure of Christ and the Christian's participation in his sacrifice.
pass_a_gloss: He will place [his] hand upon [the] head [of the] victim, and acceptable it will be. [The] hand placed communion signifies: [the things] which are offered, ours they become. Christ [the] head; we [the] members. To place [the] hand — to consent and to confess [the] sins which into [the] victim pass. [The] blood sprinkled at [the] altar: without [of] blood [the] pouring out not happens remission. [The] high priest our Christ once offered himself.

choices.why: The Latin hostia refers to the sacrificial animal; 'victim' preserves the sacrificial sense without importing later liturgical connotations.
The term denotes shared participation; 'communion' captures the theological sense of union with Christ in the offering.
The phrase echoes Hebrews 9:22; 'pouring out' is literal and preserves the physical imagery of the ritual.
The adverb semel is emphatic, contrasting Christ's single offering with repeated Levitical sacrifices; 'once' must be retained.
rejected: made a single offering of himself

pass_b_english: He will lay his hand upon the head of the victim, and it will be acceptable. The laying on of the hand signifies communion: the things that are offered become ours. Christ is the head; we are the members. To lay on the hand is to consent and to confess the sins that pass over into the victim. The blood is sprinkled at the altar: without the pouring out of blood there is no remission. Our high priest Christ offered himself once.

problems.source_quote: Pontifex noster Christus semel obtulit seipsum
problems.why: The source quotes no Scripture here; this is Origen's own statement. The English wrongly adds Hebrews 7:27 as a citation, making authorial exposition appear as biblical quotation.
problems.fix: Our high priest Christ offered himself once.
problems.ruling: Source 'Pontifex noster Christus semel obtulit seipsum' has no citation; adding Hebrews 7:27 misleads readers.

problems.source_quote: Imponet manum suam super caput hostiae, et acceptabilis erit
problems.why: No chapter-verse citation exists in the source text. Adding it supplies information the source does not claim.
problems.fix: He will lay his hand upon the head of the victim, and it will be acceptable.
problems.ruling: Source 'Imponet manum...' lacks citation; adding Leviticus 1:4 misrepresents source text.

problems.source_quote: Sanguis adspersus ad altare: sine sanguinis effusione non fit remissio
problems.why: No biblical citation appears in source; this is authorial exposition. Adding Hebrews 9:22 misrepresents the text's voice and genre.
problems.fix: The blood is sprinkled at the altar: without the pouring out of blood there is no remission.
problems.ruling: Source 'Sanguis adspersus...' lacks citation; adding Hebrews 9:22 misrepresents source text.

last_rejected.quote: the things that are offered become ours
last_rejected.why: Latin 'nostra fiunt' means 'become ours' but context shows communion: we become united with what is offered, not that offerings become our property. 'Become ours' reverses the theological direction of union with Christ.
last_rejected.fix: what is offered becomes ours, or we are joined to what is offered
last_rejected.ruling: 'quae offeruntur, nostra fiunt' literally says offered things become ours; 'become ours' is correct, not reversed.

last_rejected.why: 'Consentire' here means 'to agree together, to unite oneself with' (the victim/Christ), not merely 'to consent' as mental agreement. The theological sense of participatory union is weakened.
last_rejected.fix: to join oneself and to confess
last_rejected.ruling: 'consentire' includes 'to consent/agree'; rendering is within normal range, not a major meaning change.
